name: StatementSift — Bank Statement PDF to CSV, Converted & Reconciled (Local, Private)
description:
My bank gives me a PDF statement — how do I turn it into a CSV my accounting software can use? Your accounting software wants a CSV. And the converters that do this either charge you $29 a month in the cloud — with your statement on someone else's server — or $49.99 for a desktop tool that converts without ever checking its own work.
StatementSift converts a text-based bank statement PDF into a clean CSV on your own computer, then does what the other converters don't: it reconciles. Every running-balance step is walked and verified, and the closing balance is checked against opening + the sum of all amounts.
WHAT IT CORRECTS ON ITS OWN
• Amounts with thousands commas (2,500.00 → 2500.00) and DD/MM/YYYY dates — normalized
• Exact-duplicate transaction lines printed twice — removed, and logged
WHAT IT REPORTS — BUT NEVER SILENTLY "REPAIRS"
• Running-balance breaks: the exact line, the balance the chain requires, the balance the statement prints, and the difference
• A closing balance that does not reconcile with the opening balance plus the transactions
A balance break means one side is wrong — deciding which is a conversation with your bank, not a guess by software. Then it RE-CHECKS the cleaned CSV by re-parsing and re-verifying it independently.
VERIFIED, NOT VIBES
On a seeded test statement (6 transaction lines, 4 planted defects): 1 exact duplicate removed, 4 corrections logged, and 1 balance break caught red-handed — the statement printed 12,700.50 where the chain requires 12,695.50, a +5.00 difference that also made the closing balance fail reconciliation. The re-check confirmed 0 duplicates remained and the single break was carried honestly, not papered over.
100% LOCAL & PRIVATE — no upload, no account, no subscription. A bank statement is the most sensitive document you own; it never leaves your computer.
Windows 10/11, no other software needed. You get transactions.csv (with per-row flags) and the reconciliation report.
Scope: text-based statement PDFs (the kind you download from your bank) whose transaction lines end in "<amount> <balance>". Scanned or photographed statements need OCR and are out of scope for this build — StatementSift will tell you so instead of guessing.
